summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-react preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is identifier-obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style `_0xXXXX` symbols and dictionary-lookup indirection) and, at `npm install` time, constructs a URL of the form `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...zip`, downloads and extracts the Bun runtime binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable (`chmodSync(..., 493)`), and then `execFileSync`s that Bun binary to run the locally shipped `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-bundled file (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) containing a single scrambled string-array plus rotation function — an opaque payload that Node-based scanners cannot trace because it is executed by a separately downloaded runtime. The package is published as a deprecated React ESLint config whose only legitimate output is a flat config array from index.js; an alternate JS runtime download and execution of a large obfuscated bundle have no relation to that stated purpose. The shape (install-time alternate-runtime dropper + heavily obfuscated payload + ecosystem mismatch on a scope with legitimate history) is consistent with a trojanized release of the `@ornikar` scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
